bull_case: Mission-critical reliability, qualification and repeat utility orders support willingness to pay.
bear_case: Dual-sourcing and new supplier capacity may reduce scarcity-driven pricing.
thesis: Products solve high-cost grid bottlenecks where reliability and delivery matter. Repeat customers/backlog support value, but direct retention metrics are absent.

evidence.claim: NextEra was 15.9% and Saudi Electricity 5.0% of H1 revenue.
Backlog was ₩12.31tn after H1 revenue of ₩2.178tn.
H1 operating margin was ~25.0% with key utilization 88.8–95.1%.

falsifiers: Loss of major utility qualifications or repeated quality failures with shrinking backlog undermine the product thesis.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Growth is backed by mission-critical repeat orders, utilization and margins, not marketing/subsidy without value.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 단일 제품·단일 고객·단일 규제에 대한 치명적 종속성
hard_veto_flags.rationale: Largest disclosed H1 customer is 15.9%, below the 25% watch trigger, with multiple products/geographies.

next_checks: Track concentration, warranty provisions and win rates.

subscores.rationale: Mission-critical reliability and repeat utility orders support strong avoided-outage/delay value.
Repeat customers/backlog imply retention, but no direct cohort/wallet-share statistic exists.
~25% margin, high utilization and net cash show strong economics; growth capex prevents 90.

uncertainties.rationale: ROI inferred from mission criticality/repeat orders.
